title: One Kettlebell, Three Moves. That's a Full Home Gym
description: One kettlebell replaces half a gym, but most people lift it wrong. How to pick the weight, the three moves you need, and the detail that decides it all.
excerpt: A kettlebell isn't a weirdly shaped dumbbell. It works with momentum, and that changes the whole movement.
content:
A kettlebell is the best value in home training. One bell, half a square metre of floor, and it covers strength, conditioning and mobility at once. The catch: almost everyone makes the same three mistakes in week one.

## A kettlebell is not a dumbbell

The centre of mass sits outside the handle, so the bell pulls on every rep. Your body has to manage momentum, not just lift a load. That's exactly why a swing trains your posterior chain differently than a deadlift — it isn't the path, it's the deceleration.

The practical payoff: you learn to control a load that's already moving. That transfers to cycling, to five-a-side, to picking a kid up off the floor.

## The three moves you need

1. **Swing** — feet shoulder width, bell between them, hinge at the hip, don't squat. The power comes from the hips; your arms are just rope. 5 × 15.
2. **Goblet squat** — bell at your chest, squat down, elbows inside the knees. The fastest way to learn an upright squat, because the front load straightens you out for free.
3. **Turkish get-up** — slow, technical, you'll hate it and you need it. 3 × 3 per side. It teaches your trunk and shoulder to work as one unit.

## What weight to buy

Untrained man: 12 or 16 kg. Untrained woman: 8 or 12 kg. It sounds heavy, but a swing with a light bell is pointless — there's nothing to decelerate. Buy one size up rather than one size down.

## The detail that decides everything

Hinge, not squat. If your knees drift forward on the swing and the bell goes up because your arms lifted it, you're doing a different exercise with real risk to your lower back. Hips back, shins vertical, spine neutral.

If you're unsure, a few sessions with someone watching you is worth more than any video. A private gym you book by the hour, like [GymHome](https://gymhome.cz), is ideal for that — mirror, space, nobody waiting on your rack.

Filming your own technique breakdowns? [TubeVoice](https://tubevoice.io) dubs them into other languages, so the content works outside your market too.

Buy one bell, learn the swing properly, and you won't need anything else for three months.
